s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls with otologic abnormalities
salient_findings: Progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls over 5 days
Obstructed external ear canals with effusion and cerumen
Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals
key_facts: 4-year-old girl of Turkish ancestry
Presented to the emergency department with progressive unsteadiness and recurrent falls
Initial fall resulted in a nasal bridge laceration
No prior medical history
Alert and afebrile on examination
External ear canals obstructed by effusion and cerumen
Three-month history of ear problems
Initial diagnosis of otitis media with effusion and tympanic perforation
Partial resolution with antibiotic treatment
Current otoscopic examination showed intact left tympanic membrane and occluded right external canal
Frenzel’s examination showed no nystagmus
Contrast-enhanced CT showed bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals
Adenoid hypertrophy and mild sinus mucosal thickening
Brainstem evoked response audiometry demonstrated profound right-sided hearing loss

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and semicircular canals, and otologic abnormalities

shortlist.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar presentation to Langerhans cell histiocytosis, with osteolytic lesions

shortlist.label: Cholesteatoma
shortlist.why_kept: Occluded right external canal and polypoid tissue, consistent with cholesteatoma

shortlist.label: Mastoiditis
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids and history of ear problems

shortlist.label: Histiocytosis X
shortlist.why_kept: Similar to Langerhans cell histiocytosis, with osteolytic lesions and otologic abnormalities

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral osteolysis of the mastoids, superior and lateral semicircular canals, and the right external auditory canal, along with a separate osteolytic lesion in the dorsal left parietal bone, is highly suggestive of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, which is known to cause lytic bone lesions and can affect the temporal bone, leading to hearing loss and balance problems.

rejected.label: Eosinophilic granuloma
rejected.why: Eosinophilic granuloma is a type of Langerhans cell histiocytosis, but it is not the most comprehensive diagnosis given the multiple bone lesions and systemic involvement.

rejected.label: Cholesteatoma
rejected.why: Cholesteatoma is a type of skin cyst that can occur in the middle ear, but it does not typically cause the widespread osteolysis seen in this case.

rejected.label: Mastoiditis
rejected.why: Mastoiditis is an infection of the mastoid bone, but it does not typically cause the lytic lesions seen on the CT scan, and the patient's symptoms and examination findings are not consistent with a simple infection.

rejected.label: Histiocytosis X
rejected.why: Histiocytosis X is an outdated term that was previously used to describe Langerhans cell histiocytosis, but it is not a specific diagnosis and is no longer used in medical literature.
